html:
Prince Henry, known as the Navigator, was a son of King John I of Portugal who sponsored voyages of exploration down the west coast of Africa from the 1420s until his death in 1460.

He did not sail himself. From the Algarve he sent ships south, hoping for gold, a sea route around the Muslim world and Christian allies. His captains settled Madeira and the Azores, where sugar plantations soon grew. In 1434 Gil Eanes rounded Cape Bojador, which sailors had feared to pass. The light ship called the caravel made these voyages possible.

His ships also began the Portuguese trade in enslaved Africans: the first were sold at Lagos in 1444, an early step of the Atlantic slave trade. By his death his captains had passed Cape Verde and reached the Gambia River. The voyages led on to Vasco da Gama and to the landing in Brazil. See Portugal.
